description: Two weeks of 15-minute discharge at two USGS gauges on the Colorado River (October 2025): Lees Ferry, below Glen Canyon Dam, and near Grand Canyon (Phantom Ranch), about 141 km (87.5 river miles) downstream; USGS Water Data OGC API, no key. Signals idea: time-delay estimation by cross-correlation. Slide one record over the other and correlate at every lag; the lag where they agree best is the delay, the method behind GPS, radar, sonar and seismic location. The steps put both gauges on one clock (Polars), correlate the flows and their 15-minute changes at every lag from 0 to 48 h (a cross join of records and lags, then Pearson r per lag), pick the best lag and the runner-up, and line the records up. The aha: the dam's daily hydropeaking pulse needs about 21 hours to reach Phantom Ranch (a wave speed of about 6.6 km/h), but because the pulse repeats every day, the correlation has nearly as high a peak a day later: a periodic signal only fixes a delay modulo its period (radar's range ambiguity), and only causality and the non-periodic day-to-day changes decide. Caveats: provisional and approved USGS data mixed; tributaries (the Paria, the Little Colorado) add water, most after rain; the wave speed is the pulse's (celerity), faster than the water itself; the river distance is from the river-mile system, not measured here. Change the time range in both queries for other weeks (low-flow weekends and the spring high-flow experiments are good tests).
name: Cross-correlation: a dam's pulse down the Grand Canyon
